items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I jammed with Willie and Peanuts almost every night.

ctx.x: The band went on tour and Sidney de Paris was added which made four trumpets and gave the brass section an even bigger sound and more punch than it had before. For my money, Charlie Johnson had a band that was second to Fletcher Henderson and he used to give Fletcher some tough battles before I joined the band.

We played a few days in Buffalo and it was at a club called 'Ann Montgomery' that I met a trumpet player called 'Peanuts' Holland who was a blowing cat with a lot of technique and a big sound. Another young musician I met at this same club was a fellow named Willie Smith. I didn't know anything about Jimmie Lunceford, but Charlie Johnson wanted to hire Willie the first night he heard him. I jammed with Willie and Peanuts almost every night.

A boy that I had played with at one time in Helvey's band named John L. Henderson was working in a band at the biggest Negro hotel in Buffalo, so I went to listen to him the night before we were to leave. I had a ball and got so drunk that John L. told me that I could go to sleep in his room as he was also living in the hotel.
